extra.message: An HTTP response construction serializes caught exception detail (message) without normalization, disclosing internal diagnostic information to the client.
Credential material passed to a project-local fast/broken digest helper — use bcrypt/scrypt/argon2.

An HTTP response discloses data the caller is not entitled to receive: GET /all returns every row from SELECT * FROM users, and the users table stores password_hash and session_id, so the response body discloses authentication hashes and session identifiers for all users without projection or redaction.
Password stored or matched in cleartext — no hashing is applied anywhere in this module; use bcrypt/scrypt/argon2.

This authentication, registration or account-recovery surface answers differently (error wording) depending on whether the submitted account identifier resolves to an existing account, so an attacker can enumerate valid accounts by probing identifiers alone.

A state-changing GET operation is reachable with browser-attached session credentials and enforces no CSRF token, origin binding, or equivalent proof of user intent.
Hand-rolled cookie session token carries no expiry component at all, so a captured cookie authenticates forever.
Session teardown removes only the client-side cookie; the authoritative server-side session record is never deleted, so a previously captured credential keeps authenticating.
'APP_SECRET' embeds key material consumed by a cryptographic operation.
